title: Claude Opus stopped an OCR model's repetition loops by editing 0.0085% of its weights, no training, for about $10 of HF Jobs compute
summary: Daniel van Strien asked Claude Opus to find a small OCR model and fix its repetition doom loops, with a budget of 5 hours and $100 on Hugging Face Jobs. Opus changed 0.0085% of the weights without any training, and the model now reads an 1881 page it used to answer with 16,399 characters of dots. It took under 3 hours and about $10 of compute.

appearances.title: Weight edit cuts an OCR model's repetition loops
appearances.summary: Daniel van Strien had Claude Opus edit an OCR model with no training, changing 0.0085% of the weights so a page that had produced 16,399 characters of dots was read instead. On 2,165 pages of historic books, runaway loops went from 3 to 1 and errors on an 1881 volume fell 38%. Hugging Face reposted it.
